# Releasing CodeScene for JetBrains

Releases are created by pushing annotated Git tags. GitHub Actions validates the tag, builds the plugin with the tagged version, creates the GitHub release with generated notes, and, for stable releases, publishes to JetBrains Marketplace once the tagged commit has a green `Build` run.

## Stable releases

Tag the `master` merge commit that should be released and push the tag. No version bump, notes edit or release commit is needed beforehand:

```bash
git tag -a vX.Y.Z -m "Release vX.Y.Z"
git push origin vX.Y.Z
```

Tag the merge commit that has a green `Build` run. After every stable release the workflow pushes a `chore(release): set pluginVersion to X.Y.Z` commit to `master`; that bot commit never gets a `Build` run, so tag the merge commit below it, not the bot commit.

The release is admitted only when all of these hold:

- the tag is annotated;
- the tag is exactly `vX.Y.Z` (no leading zeros, no suffix);
- the tagged commit is on `master`;
- the version is newer than every published stable GitHub release, including releases that were created but not yet promoted to latest. Skipping versions is allowed.

A tag that fails admission stops the workflow before anything is built or published. Delete the tag, fix the cause and push a new one.

## What the workflow does

The `Release` workflow runs on every pushed `v*` tag and can be started manually with `workflow_dispatch` (see Recovery). Releases are serialized: runs queue one after another instead of cancelling or overlapping each other. The jobs run in this order:

1. `metadata` validates the tag against the admission rules and resolves the version, whether it is a test release, the notes range, the stable baseline and the tagged commit.
2. `build` builds the plugin with the tagged version (`-PreleaseVersion`), verifies the plugin descriptor version and stores the ZIP as a workflow artifact. It has no signing or publishing secrets.
3. `create-release` generates the release notes and creates the GitHub release, or edits it if it already exists. Test releases are prereleases. Releases are created as not latest.
4. `upload` attaches the ZIP to the release unless an asset with that name is already attached.
5. `test-gate` (stable only) requires a successful `Build` run for the tagged commit.
6. `publish` (stable only) rebuilds the plugin and publishes it to JetBrains Marketplace. This is the only job that has the signing and Marketplace secrets.
7. `record-version` (stable only) writes `pluginVersion` on `master` through the bot commit. `pluginVersion` on `master` is the last released version and is written only by this bot; never edit it by hand.
8. `promote` (stable only) marks the release as latest.

A stable release becomes the latest release only after it has been published and its version has been recorded. Test releases run `metadata`, `build`, `create-release` and `upload` only: no gate, no publish, no commit, never latest.

## Release notes

Release notes are generated by GitHub from the pull requests merged since the previous stable release, using `.github/release.yml`. The comparison range is:

- stable releases compare with the previous stable release that is an ancestor of the tag;
- the first test release for a version compares with the latest stable release;
- later test releases for the same version compare with the preceding test release for that version.

Test releases also begin with a link comparing the latest stable release with the test tag.

Pull requests are grouped by label. Labels are optional; a pull request without a matching label lands in Other Changes.

| Category         | Labels                                  |
| ---------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| Breaking Changes | `breaking-change`, `breaking`           |
| Features         | `feature`, `enhancement`                |
| Bug Fixes        | `bug`, `fix`, `defect`                  |
| Security         | `security`                              |
| Documentation    | `documentation`, `docs`                 |
| Dependencies     | `dependencies`                          |
| Other Changes    | any other label, or no label            |

Pull requests labelled `ignore-for-release` or `skip-changelog`, and pull requests authored by `dependabot` or `github-actions`, are left out of the notes.

Notes are regenerated every time the `create-release` job runs, including on recovery re-runs, which overwrites any hand edits made to the release body. Adjust labels on the pull requests and re-run the release instead of editing notes by hand.

## Recovery

Every job is safe to re-run. To retry, re-run the failed jobs of the workflow run, or start the `Release` workflow manually from `master` with the existing tag as the `tag` input. A manual run uses the tooling on `master`, so it also recovers tags created before a tooling fix.

- `create-release` edits the existing release instead of failing, and regenerates its notes.
- `upload` skips assets that are already attached.
- `test-gate` is evaluated again on every run.
- `publish` treats a Marketplace response saying it `already contains version` as published.
- `record-version` never lowers `pluginVersion` on `master`; if `master` is already at or above the version it does nothing.
- `promote` never moves latest off a newer release.

Gate failures:

- No `Build` run found: the tag is on a commit without one, typically the bot's `chore(release)` commit. Delete the tag and tag the merge commit below it.
- `Build` still running: wait for it to finish, then re-run the release.
- `Build` failed or was cancelled, for example by a follow-up push cancelling the run: re-run `Build` for the tagged commit until it passes, then re-run the release.

## Abandoning a stable release

Before `publish` has succeeded, delete the release together with its tag:

```bash
gh release delete vX.Y.Z --cleanup-tag
```

Do this rather than leaving the release behind: an unpromoted stable release still counts for tag admission, as the base of `make test-release` and as the start of the next release's notes range.

Once `publish` has succeeded the version is on JetBrains Marketplace and cannot be withdrawn by deleting the tag. Complete that release by re-running the remaining jobs instead.

## Test releases

Test releases are GitHub prereleases for testers. The default increment is patch:

```bash
make test-release
```

Minor and major test releases can be requested explicitly:

```bash
make test-release BUMP=patch
make test-release BUMP=minor
make test-release BUMP=major
```

The command needs an authenticated `gh`. It takes the base from the highest published stable GitHub release, applies the increment, appends `-test.<short-sha>`, and creates an annotated tag such as `v0.5.11-test.a1b2c3d` on the current commit. It does not change any file.

Push the exact tag printed by the command:

```bash
git push origin v0.5.11-test.a1b2c3d
```

GitHub Actions verifies that:

- the tag matches `vX.Y.Z-test.<hex-sha>`;
- the SHA suffix identifies the tagged commit;
- the test base is exactly the next patch, minor, or major version after the highest published stable release.

The test version is injected with `-PreleaseVersion`, so the ZIP filename and plugin descriptor both contain the full test version. Test builds are GitHub prereleases, are not gated on `Build`, are never marked as the latest release, and are never published to JetBrains Marketplace. The tagged commit does not need to be on `master`.

A branch that does not yet contain this release flow still runs its old workflow for test tags until `master` is merged into it.

### Installing a test release

1. Open the test release on the repository's GitHub Releases page.
2. Download `CodeScene-X.Y.Z-test.<short-sha>.zip`.
3. In the JetBrains IDE, open **Settings | Plugins**.
4. Open the gear menu and choose **Install Plugin from Disk**.
5. Select the downloaded ZIP and restart the IDE if requested.
6. Open the CodeScene plugin details in **Settings | Plugins** and verify that the displayed version matches the GitHub tag.

Artifacts uploaded by the regular build workflow are CI diagnostics. Tagged GitHub prereleases are the supported tester distribution channel.

## Changelog history

Releases made before this flow have their notes in the former changelog file, which is no longer in the repository. Copy that history onto the matching GitHub releases with the migration script. It reads the file from the git history by default.

Run a dry run first; it lists what would change and updates nothing:

```bash
bb --classpath .github -m migrate-changelog
```

Then apply it:

```bash
bb --classpath .github -m migrate-changelog --apply
```

The script appends each section to the matching stable release under a marked block, so running it again is safe and only updates releases whose block differs. Use `--file <path>` to read the history from a file instead of git, and `--repo <owner/name>` to target another repository.

## Requirements

- [Babashka](https://babashka.org) for `make test-release`, the release tooling and the migration script.
- An authenticated [GitHub CLI](https://cli.github.com) (`gh`) for `make test-release`, the migration script and manual recovery.
- No personal access token is used. The workflow runs with the repository `GITHUB_TOKEN`, and the bot push in `record-version` relies on `master` not enforcing a branch ruleset that blocks it.
